    86	\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}
    87	
    88	Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
    89	The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
    90	$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
    91	$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
    92	players and every line pair, define a POVM by
    93	\[
    94	 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
    95	 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
    96	\]
    97	There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
    98	requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
    99	uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
   100	evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
   101	outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.
   102	
   103	The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
   104	joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
   105	defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
   106	$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
   107	the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
   108	answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
   109	distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
   110	family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
   111	\begin{align*}
   112	 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
   113	 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   114	 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
   115	 &=4.
   116	\end{align*}
   117	The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
   118	is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
   119	the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
   120	polynomially small functions of $\eps$.
   121	
   122	For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
   123	\[
   124	 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   125	    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
   126	 \qquad
   127	 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
   128	    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
   129	\]
   130	The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
   131	assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
   132	difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
   133	$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
   134	admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
   135	enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
   136	vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.

   215	\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}
   216	
   217	The same quantitative omission remains in the auxiliary
   218	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
   219	function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
   220	at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does
   221	not remove this obstruction. The first-route estimate
   222	$C m g(\eps,md/q)$ in
   223	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness} has the same
   224	problem: it still tends to zero at $\eps=0$ with fixed $m,d$ and increasing $q$.
   225	These unrestricted auxiliaries are tracked by \ghissue{509} and \ghissue{511},
   226	respectively. The source instead uses the family constructed by its point lemma,
   227	with $\delta_Q=\poly(\eps)$, and defines the scalar answer by
   228	$c=\alpha a+\beta b$. Claim~17-1 explicitly retains the point error.
   229	\footnote{The source passages are \path{lem:qld-4-10}, \path{lem:qld-4-12}, and
   230	\path{claim:17-1} in
   231	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   232	lines~689--709, 993--1018, and 1140--1173.}
   233	
   234	Take $m=d=1$, $\eps=0$, and let $q=2^{2k+1}>2$ tend to infinity.
   235	These parameters are admissible. The Pauli basis test has a perfect projective strategy by
   236	\path{lem:pauli-completeness}.\footnote{See
   237	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   238	lines~1229--1421, for the construction; the statement and its projective Pauli
   239	measurements appear at lines~1232--1255.}
   240	Let $\hat\psi$ be its normalized expanded state. On each player's expanded
   241	local space, define the supplied joint point measurement by
   242	\[
   243	 Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
   244	 \begin{cases}
   245	   \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
   246	   0,&\text{otherwise}.
   247	 \end{cases}
   248	\]
   249	This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
   250	every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
   251	two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
   252	maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
   253	point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.
   254	
   255	The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
   256	indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
   257	of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
   258	On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
   259	in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
   260	parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
   261	has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
   262	two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
   263	most $2/q$.
   264	
   265	This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
   266	be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
   267	player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and
   268	$\sum_p w_p=1$; the axis-degree field makes $w_p=0$ for higher-degree answers.
   269	The opposite point effect is deterministically the identity at $\alpha x^2$,
   270	so the agreement is precisely the $w_p$-weighted average of those root-count
   271	fractions. These weights depend on the line but not on $x$ along it. Averaging
   272	over the fixed coordinates, and using nonnegativity of the defect on the
   273	remaining question branches, gives for either player orientation
   274	\[
   275	 \operatorname{defect}\ \ge\
   276	 \frac18\left(1-\frac1q\right)\left(1-\frac2q\right).
   277	\]
   278	There is no undefined evaluation on these nonzero axis directions, so the
   279	completed answer alphabet does not change this calculation. The scalar field
   280	identification preserves the polynomial evaluations and their root counts.
   281	
   282	The lower bound tends to $1/8$. In contrast, the predicate
   283	\path{IsPolyErr}\textsubscript{2} bounds the proposed error at these parameters by
   284	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(0,1/q)\le Cq^{-s}$ with $s>0$, which tends to zero.
   285	For the first-route estimate, the polynomial-error bound on $g$ likewise gives
   286	fixed constants $K\ge1$ and $r,s>0$ with
   287	$C g(0,1/q)\le CKq^{-s}\longrightarrow0$.
   288	Consequently both unrestricted supplied-point auxiliaries are false,
   289	independently of the printed-error discrepancy and the diagonal-line degeneracy.
   290	This argument does not refute the existential point-witness declarations or the source
   291	\path{lem:qld-4-13}; neither requires a line approximation to every arbitrarily
   292	chosen point family.

   295	projective joint family admits some finite witness error, and a coefficient
   296	answer with zero quadratic coefficient agrees with a nonzero multiple of the
   297	square function with probability at most $2/q$.\footnote{The declarations are

    51	  cases line with

    53	    let sample : DirectLdSpace params := ⟨base, index, 0⟩

    42	      (evalOpt sample.2.1 (projX (directPointToPauli params point)) polynomials.1,

    47	        ((directEvalOpt sample.1 point

   319	private theorem linePolynomial_natDegree_le_of_coefficients {Scalar : Type*}

   322	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients polynomial).natDegree ≤ degree := by
   323	  apply Polynomial.natDegree_sum_le_of_forall_le
   324	  intro index _
   325	  by_cases hindex : index.val ≤ degree
   326	  · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   327	    have hpower := Polynomial.natDegree_pow_le
   328	      (p := (Polynomial.X : Polynomial Scalar)) (n := index.val)
   329	    simp only [Polynomial.natDegree_X, Nat.mul_one] at hpower
   330	    simpa using hpower.trans hindex

   334	private theorem affine_comp_natDegree_le {Scalar : Type*} [Field Scalar]
   335	    (polynomial : Polynomial Scalar) (offset slope : Scalar) {degree : ℕ}
   336	    (hdegree : polynomial.natDegree ≤ degree) :
   337	    (polynomial.comp (Polynomial.C offset + Polynomial.C slope * Polynomial.X)).natDegree ≤
   338	      degree := by
   339	  have haffine : (Polynomial.C offset + Polynomial.C slope * Polynomial.X).natDegree ≤ 1 := by
   340	    refine (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
   341	    · simp
   342	    · exact Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans (by simp)

   346	either the two scalar coordinates are constant, or both projected parameters
   347	are constant. This is the algebraic assertion at paper lines 1127--1132. -/
   348	theorem combineLinePoly_axis_degree {Scalar : Type*} [Field Scalar] {bound degree : ℕ}
   349	    (hdegree : 1 ≤ degree) (data : Fin 8 → Scalar)
   350	    (polynomialX polynomialZ : Fin (bound + 1) → Scalar)
   351	    (hdegreeX : ∀ index, degree < index.val → polynomialX index = 0)
   352	    (hdegreeZ : ∀ index, degree < index.val → polynomialZ index = 0)
   353	    (haxis : (data 5 = 0 ∧ data 7 = 0) ∨ (data 1 = 0 ∧ data 3 = 0)) :
   354	    ∀ index : Fin (bound + 1 + 1), degree < index.val →
   355	      combineLinePoly (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3)
   356	        (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7) polynomialX polynomialZ index = 0 := by
   357	  have hpolyX := linePolynomial_natDegree_le_of_coefficients polynomialX hdegreeX
   358	  have hpolyZ := linePolynomial_natDegree_le_of_coefficients polynomialZ hdegreeZ
   359	  have htotal : (combineLinePolynomial (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3)
   360	      (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7) polynomialX polynomialZ).natDegree ≤ degree := by
   361	    unfold combineLinePolynomial
   362	    rcases haxis with ⟨halpha, hbeta⟩ | ⟨hparamX, hparamZ⟩
   363	    · simp only [halpha, hbeta, Polynomial.C_0, zero_mul, add_zero]
   364	      refine (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
   365	      · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   366	        simpa only [Polynomial.natDegree_C, Nat.zero_add] using
   367	          (affine_comp_natDegree_le _ (data 0) (data 1) hpolyX)
   368	      · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   369	        simpa only [Polynomial.natDegree_C, Nat.zero_add] using
   370	          (affine_comp_natDegree_le _ (data 2) (data 3) hpolyZ)
   371	    · simp only [hparamX, hparamZ, Polynomial.C_0, zero_mul, add_zero, Polynomial.comp_C]

   373	          ((Polynomial.C constant + Polynomial.C slope * Polynomial.X) *
   374	            Polynomial.C value).natDegree ≤ degree := by
   375	        refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   376	        simp only [Polynomial.natDegree_C, Nat.add_zero]

   378	          (Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans (by simpa using hdegree)))
   379	      exact (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le (hterm _ _ _) (hterm _ _ _))

   394	private theorem affine_slope_eq_zero {Scalar : Type*} [Field Scalar] {dimension : ℕ}

   408	    let data := sublines.affineData sample hsample

   414	      coordinateDirection sample.1.index := by
   415	    rcases sample with ⟨line, pair⟩
   416	    cases line with

   418	    | diagonal => cases haxis
   419	  by_cases hspecial : sample.1.index = alphaVar params.m ∨ sample.1.index = betaVar params.m

   441	    rw [← hcompat.2.1, ← hcompat.2.2.2.1, hcoordinate]

175:### Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`
176-
177:`\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.
178-
179:**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.
180-
181:**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).

183:A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.

\section{At a glance}

\textbf{Difficulty.} The domain correction is elementary; the remaining
formal estimate requires the project's state-dependent Cauchy--Schwarz and
restricted-distribution arguments. \textbf{Estimated weight.} The correction
affects two Lean modules and their blueprint correspondence. It retains the
unfinished scalar estimate. The pasting consistency construction has been
recovered separately. \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite sums, positivity, and real
square roots use Mathlib; the measurement construction and subline law use
the local quantum API. \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Completeness of a
POVM, projectivity, and Cauchy--Schwarz suffice for the counterexample and
the proposed source proof. The counterexample below is a mathematical
calculation, not a kernel-certified Lean instance.

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
\begin{align*}
 A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
 B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
\end{align*}
The paper's Claim 17-2 states
\[
 |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
 \quad\text{for}\quad
 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.

\section{The construction used by the source}

The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
over the Z polynomial:
\[
 \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: scripts/install_git_hooks.sh [--install|--check|--help]

Install or verify the repository-local Git hooks for the current worktree.

  --install  Set core.hooksPath to .githooks. This is the default.
  --check    Verify that core.hooksPath points to .githooks and hooks are executable.
  --help     Show this help text.
EOF
}

MODE="install"
case "${1:-}" in
  ""|--install)
    MODE="install"
    ;;
  --check|--verify)
    MODE="check"
    ;;
  --help|-h)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    usage >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"

if [ ! -d .githooks ]; then
  echo "No .githooks directory found at repository root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

check_hook_files() {
  HOOK_STATUS=0
  for HOOK in .githooks/pre-commit .githooks/pre-push .githooks/reference-transaction
  do
    if [ ! -f "$HOOK" ]; then
      echo "Missing hook file: $HOOK" >&2
      HOOK_STATUS=1
    elif [ ! -x "$HOOK" ]; then
      echo "Hook file is not executable: $HOOK" >&2
      HOOK_STATUS=1
    fi
  done
  return "$HOOK_STATUS"
}

check_hooks_installed() {
  INSTALL_STATUS=0
  CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH="$(git config --get core.hooksPath || true)"
  case "$CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH" in
    .githooks|"$ROOT/.githooks")
      ;;
    "")
      echo "core.hooksPath is not set for this worktree." >&2
      INSTALL_STATUS=1
      ;;
    *)
      echo "core.hooksPath is '$CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH', not .githooks." >&2
      INSTALL_STATUS=1
      ;;
  esac

  if ! check_hook_files; then
    INSTALL_STATUS=1
  fi

  if [ "$INSTALL_STATUS" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE Git hooks are installed for this worktree."
    echo "core.hooksPath=$CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH"
  else
    echo "Run scripts/install_git_hooks.sh to install the repository hooks." >&2
  fi
  return "$INSTALL_STATUS"
}

if [ "$MODE" = "check" ]; then
  check_hooks_installed
  exit $?
fi

chmod +x .githooks/pre-commit .githooks/pre-push .githooks/reference-transaction
git config core.hooksPath .githooks

echo "Installed MIPStarRE Git hooks by setting core.hooksPath to .githooks."
echo "Verify with scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check."
echo "Set MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1 for a one-off bypass of the tooling checks (the workflow-layer line budget and merge-loss guard still run)."
echo "Set MIPSTARRE_HOOK_FULL=1 when invoking local/bin/checked-push.sh for the full local gate."

Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"
HOOK_ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS="$(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)"

run_without_git_local_env() (
  # Git exports repository-local variables while running hooks.  Several script
  # tests create temporary repositories; keep those tests independent of this
  # checkout.
  unset $GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS
  "$@"
)

# A merge commit can be syntactically valid while its index has been reset to
# the first-parent tree.  That failure mode silently discarded clean incoming
# additions on issue-109 and issue-110 (issue #222).  Check the pending index
# before every other gate, including the documented blanket hook bypass: a
# missing incoming path is valid only when the branch deleted a base path.
MERGE_HEAD_PATH="$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking the merge result for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" --repo "$ROOT"
fi

# Scope-control guard (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild):
# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=1000 changed lines per commit (400 until the owner raised it on 2026-09-05).  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# by the OWNER per commit, never self-granted by an agent session.  Runs
# before the ACMR early-exit so deletion-only commits are counted too
# (numstat includes deletions; PR 7 round 3, F8), and before the
# MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS exit so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the
# owner-only budget override.
# A merge that carries main stages already-reviewed content.  A merge head
# contained in github/main measures the budget against MERGE_HEAD; a merge head
# that contains github/main (a parent branch of a stack that already merged
# main; owner decision 2026-09-05) measures it against github/main, so inherited
# main content counts zero while the PR's cumulative workflow diff and any
# side-branch content beyond main still count.  Any other side-branch merge
# stays budgeted against HEAD.
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor MERGE_HEAD refs/remotes/github/main 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: main-history merge; budget measured against MERGE_HEAD."
elif [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/github/main MERGE_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/github/main)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge carrying github/main; workflow-layer content beyond github/main is budgeted."
else
  BUDGET_BASE=""
  if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge; workflow-layer merge content is budgeted."
  fi
fi
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat $BUDGET_BASE -- local/ .githooks/ \
  scripts/tests/test_dispatch.py scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py \
  scripts/tests/test_lake_root.py scripts/tests/test_pre_push_hook.py \

Blueprint ``\leanok`` axiom-closure checker. This script audits the blueprint
chapters against the Lean codebase. For each unique declaration referenced by
``\lean{...}`` in ``blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex`` it: * checks that the
declaration exists in the Lean source tree; * if any blueprint entry for that
declaration carries ``\leanok`` on the statement or proof, runs ``#print
axioms`` and fails on any transitive dependency on ``sorryAx``; * optionally
warns when a blueprint declaration is sorry-free in Lean but lacks any
``\leanok`` tag (enable ``--warn-missing-leanok``). The checker imports only
the Lean modules that define the referenced blueprint declarations, rather
than importing the top-level ``MIPStarRE`` barrel. This keeps the rebuild
scope small and avoids stale-barrel issues. Use ``--skip-axiom-check`` for a
fast parse-only smoke test. Use ``--ci`` to exit with status 1 when any
``\leanok`` declaration fails the axiom audit.

  --ci                  Exit with status 1 when any \leanok declaration fails

usage: check_blueprint_latex.py [-h] [--root ROOT]

Check blueprint LaTeX source conventions. The blueprint intentionally avoids
``cleveref``. The original paper uses ``\Cref`` and related commands
extensively, but the blueprint should spell out the reference type explicitly
and then use ordinary ``\ref`` or ``\eqref``. This keeps the print and web
builds independent of ``cleveref``. Remark environments are also expository,
not proof-bearing blueprint nodes. They should not carry ``\lean{}``,
``\leanok``, or ``\uses{}`` metadata; such metadata belongs on definitions,
lemmas, propositions, theorems, and corollaries. Labels declared inside
remarks should likewise not occur as targets of ``\uses{}``, since a remark is
not a theorem-like dependency. This rule is semantic in the modest sense
needed here: it follows the labels actually declared in remark environments,
rather than relying on a naming convention such as a ``rem:`` prefix.

usage: audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py [-h] [--root ROOT] [--json] [--ci]
                                        [--broad-vocabulary] [--warn-only]
                                        [--include-informational-envs]

Audit paper-facing blueprint statements for proof-debt inputs. The faithful-
formalization policy allows auxiliary bridge or repair lemmas, but a Lean
declaration advertised as a paper theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary
should not acquire an additional public hypothesis whose purpose is to supply
an unproved part of the proof. This script is a conservative review aid for
that boundary: * read theorem-like ``\lean{...}`` references from the active
blueprint; * resolve those references to public Lean declarations under
``MIPStarRE/``; * inspect only the public input portion of the declaration
header after the declaration name and before the result type; * report
occurrences of blocking proof-debt vocabulary such as ``BridgeHypotheses``,
``Residual``, ``RepairInput``, ``Package``, ``Bundle``, ``Conditional``,
``Producer``, ``Obligation``, an ``Input`` bundle, a wrapper, an
``Unfaithful`` marker type, or a generic ``Hypotheses`` / ``Assumptions``
bundle; * with ``--broad-vocabulary``, also report the wider tracker
vocabulary ``Statement``, ``Output``, ``Conclusion``, ``Witness``, ``Data``,
and ``Compatibility`` in public inputs. This mode is an inventory tool while
those broad occurrences are classified and reduced; it is deliberately not the
default blocking gate. * classify quoted external theorem interfaces
separately in broad mode, so external citations from the overview are not
conflated with internal proof obligations. * reject paper-facing blueprint
entries that point to declaration names with conditional proof-debt forms such
as ``*_of...Obligations``, ``*_of...Residual``, ``*_of...Repair``,
``*_of...Bundle``, ``*_of...Unfaithful``, ``*_assuming...``,
``conditional...``, or ``Conditional...``, even when the declaration header
itself has no suspicious public input. * classify known faithful boundary-
input packages separately, with paper citations, so they do not become
indistinguishable from proof debt. * optionally, with ``--include-
informational-envs``, scan ``definition``, ``remark``, and ``example`` entries
as a report-only frontier. This mode is useful for finding Lean-only
construction records advertised near a paper proof without turning those
construction records into paper theorem statements. The audit is report-only
by default. With ``--ci`` it exits non-zero when a finding is present, unless
``--warn-only`` is also supplied.
